clean_source_blocks.text: Nearly 17,000 injured and thousands more are listed as missing amid calls by UN and president Delcy Rodríguez for financial help The death toll in Venezuela’s devastating twin earthquakes has topped 4,000, the government said on Friday. At least 4,118 people were killed and 16,740 injured in the back-to-back quakes on 24 June that flattened entire districts in the coastal state of La Guaira, Venezuelan parliament chief Jorge Rodriguez wrote on Telegram. Thousands more are listed as missing. Continue reading...

Nearly 17,000 injured and thousands more are listed as missing amid calls by UN and president Delcy Rodríguez for financial help The death toll in Venezuela’s devastating twin earthquakes has topped 4,000, the government said on Friday. At least 4,118 people were killed and 16,740 injured in the back-to-back quakes on 24 June that flattened entire districts in the coastal state of La Guaira, Venezuelan parliament chief Jorge Rodriguez wrote on Telegram. Thousands more are listed as missing. A 7.5-magnitude quake – the biggest in Venezuela in over a century – struck 39 seconds after a 7.2-magnitude shock, flattening entire high-rise apartment blocks. Although rescue teams have halted searches for survivors, family members continue to scour the ruins for their loved ones, in the hope of giving them a dignified burial.

At least 920 people have been confirmed dead and tens of thousands remain missing in the aftermath of a powerful double earthquake in Venezuela. The magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes – the most powerful earthquakes to hit the country in more than a century – struck within 39 seconds of each other west of the capital Caracas. Acting president Delcy Rodriguez said on Friday that at least 2,980 people had been injured, while nearly 50,000 remain missing. Ms Rodriguez said that La Guaira, the coastal state that took the brunt of the devastation, would be put under military control in an effort to cope with the disaster. The area is located approximately 20 miles (30km) away from Caracas, which was also hit by the quakes.

On Friday, a 3.0-magnitude quake in central Caracas caused momentary panic and led to buildings being evacuated. The scale of the recovery effort facing Venezuela, where state services have been severely degraded by a prolonged economic crisis, is huge. The United Nations on Wednesday issued an urgent appeal for nearly $300m towards earthquake relief operations to assist 1.3 million people in urgent need of aid in the South American country where non-governmental organisations until recently were targets of government repression. Mobile kitchens and clinics as well as field hospitals now dot public spaces in the northern state of La Guaira, where most of the devastation occurred. The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction has estimated direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure around $37bn.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Nearly 17,000 injured and thousands more are listed as missing amid calls by UN and president Delcy Rodríguez for financial help

The death toll in Venezuela’s devastating twin earthquakes has topped 4,000, the government said on Friday.

At least 4,118 people were killed and 16,740 injured in the back-to-back quakes on 24 June that flattened entire districts in the coastal state of La Guaira, Venezuelan parliament chief Jorge Rodriguez wrote on Telegram. Thousands more are listed as missing.

A 7.5-magnitude quake – the biggest in Venezuela in over a century – struck 39 seconds after a 7.2-magnitude shock, flattening entire high-rise apartment blocks.

Although rescue teams have halted searches for survivors, family members continue to scour the ruins for their loved ones, in the hope of giving them a dignified burial.

On Friday, a 3.0-magnitude quake in central Caracas caused momentary panic and led to buildings being evacuated.

The scale of the recovery effort facing Venezuela, where state services have been severely degraded by a prolonged economic crisis, is huge.

The United Nations on Wednesday issued an urgent appeal for nearly $300m towards earthquake relief operations to assist 1.3 million people in urgent need of aid in the South American country where non-governmental organisations until recently were targets of government repression. Mobile kitchens and clinics as well as field hospitals now dot public spaces in the northern state of La Guaira, where most of the devastation occurred.

The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction has estimated direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure around $37bn.

Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has called for the release of frozen assets held abroad to be used towards the recovery.

On Wednesday she said she asked King Charles III to release about 30 tons of Venezuelan gold frozen under UK sanctions.

Delcy Rodríguez has defended her country’s emergency response to the twin earthquakes, vowing the country would not descend into social unrest.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger at what they see as the US-backed government’s inadequate response to the disaster before international teams arrived.

With Agence France-Presse and Associated Press

---

[Lähde: New York Post]
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Harrowing new aerial footage shows the quake-ravaged landscape of Venezuela as a massive international rescue effort gets underway amid a rapidly rising death toll, which officials said has topped 900.

The heartbreaking drone video features massive residential buildings reduced to rubble along the port city of La Guaira, one of the hardest-hit areas of the country, with before-and-after shots highlighting the devastation.

At least 920 have died and 3,360 were injured in the tragedy, authorities said, but the United States Geological Survey said there’s a 40% chance the death toll could climb to 10,000 and a 30% chance it will eclipse 100,000.

President Trump pledged the US would provide whatever support Venezuela needed in the immediate aftermath of the disaster, and the State Department soon thereafter announced it was sending $150 million in aid.

US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) announced Friday that Urban Search and Rescue teams based in Los Angeles and Fairfax, Va., are being transported by two US Air Force C-17 Globemaster aircraft, while a US Air Force C-17 is delivering load-movement equipment to Caracas.

“US Marine Corps MV-22 Ospreys will transport an airfield assessment team to Venezuela to support airport operations that were impacted near the earthquake epicenter,” it added.

Meanwhile, USS Fort Lauderdale and USS Billings have already arrived in waters near Venezuela to help, according to SOUTHCOM. Three US Army CH-47 Chinooks and crews from Joint Task Force-Bravo are set to leave Honduras to support the transport of key personnel and supplies that are helping the South American country.

“The command’s US Space Force component is providing satellite imagery of devastated areas to disaster relief planners in Venezuela to aid them in assessing where immediate life-saving and aid efforts are needed most and identifying what capability requests to prioritize,” SOUTHCOM added.

Neighboring countries have also been pitching in for the rescue effort.

Venezuelan neighbor Colombia said it was sending humanitarian aid along with more than 60 rescuers and four dogs, while Chile has sent a specialized Urban Search and Rescue unit of its fire department, Reuters reports.

El Salvador has dispatched some 300 rescuers and paramedics, and is sending 50 metric tons of humanitarian aid to the country. Panama has said it will send a ⁠rescue mission ​to Venezuela.

payload.title: Venezuelan kaksoisjäristysten kuolonuhrien määrä nousi yli 4 000:n
payload.summary: Kesäkuun kaksoisjäristyksissä on kuollut ainakin 4 118 ihmistä ja loukkaantunut 16 740. YK hakee lähes 300 miljoonaa dollaria avustustoimiin.
payload.content:
Venezuelassa 24. kesäkuuta tapahtuneiden kahden voimakkaan maanjäristyksen kuolonuhrien määrä on noussut ainakin 4 118:aan. Hallituksen mukaan loukkaantuneita on 16 740 ja tuhansia ihmisiä on edelleen kateissa. Pahimmat tuhot kärsinyt La Guairan rannikko-osavaltio sijaitsee noin 30 kilometrin päässä pääkaupunki Caracasista.

## Järistykset iskivät 39 sekunnin välein

Ensimmäisen järistyksen voimakkuus oli 7,2. Sitä seurasi vain 39 sekuntia myöhemmin 7,5 magnitudin järistys, joka oli Venezuelan voimakkain yli sataan vuoteen. Järistykset iskivät Caracasin länsipuolelle ja romahduttivat La Guairassa kokonaisia korkeita asuinrakennuksia. Venezuelan parlamentin johtaja Jorge Rodriguez ilmoitti uusimmat kuolonuhrien ja loukkaantuneiden määrät Telegramissa perjantaina.

La Guairassa tuhoutui kokonaisia kaupunginosia. Pelastusryhmät ovat lopettaneet eloonjääneiden etsinnät, mutta kadonneiden omaiset jatkavat raunioiden tutkimista löytääkseen läheisensä ja voidakseen haudata heidät. Viranomaiset ovat määränneet pahoin vaurioituneen osavaltion sotilaalliseen valvontaan katastrofin seurausten hallitsemiseksi.

Perjantaina myös Caracasin keskustassa tapahtui voimakkuudeltaan 3,0:n järistys. Se aiheutti hetkellistä paniikkia ja johti rakennusten evakuointeihin. Pääkaupunkikin kärsi kesäkuun kaksoisjäristyksistä, vaikka suurin osa tuhoista keskittyi pohjoisessa sijaitsevaan La Guairaan.

## YK hakee rahoitusta 1,3 miljoonan auttamiseen

YK esitti keskiviikkona kiireellisen vetoomuksen lähes 300 miljoonan dollarin keräämiseksi maanjäristyksen avustusoperaatioihin. Järjestön mukaan kiireellistä apua tarvitsee Venezuelassa noin 1,3 miljoonaa ihmistä. La Guairan julkisille alueille on perustettu siirrettäviä keittiöitä ja klinikoita sekä kenttäsairaaloita loukkaantuneiden ja kotinsa menettäneiden auttamiseksi.

Jälleenrakennusta vaikeuttaa Venezuelan pitkään jatkunut talouskriisi, joka on heikentänyt valtion palveluja jo ennen katastrofia. YK:n katastrofiriskien vähentämiseen keskittyvä toimisto arvioi asuntojen ja infrastruktuurin suorien fyysisten vahinkojen olevan noin 37 miljardia dollaria. Presidentti Delcy Rodríguez ja YK ovat vedonneet taloudellisen avun saamiseksi, kun maa valmistautuu pitkäkestoiseen asuntojen, julkisten palvelujen ja muun infrastruktuurin jälleenrakentamiseen.

Voimakkuudeltaan 7,2:n ja 7,5:n järistykset tapahtuivat 39 sekunnin välein.
YK hakee lähes 300 miljoonaa dollaria 1,3 miljoonan kiireellisesti apua tarvitsevan ihmisen auttamiseen.

YK:n katastrofiriskien vähentämiseen keskittyvä toimisto arvioi asuntojen ja infrastruktuurin suorien fyysisten vahinkojen olevan noin 37 miljardia dollaria. Nearly 17,000 injured and thousands more are listed as missing amid calls by UN and president Delcy Rodríguez for financial help The death toll in Venezuela’s devastating twin earthquakes has topped 4,000, the government said on Friday. At least 4,118 people were killed and 16,740 injured in the back-to-back quakes on 24 June that flattened entire districts in the coastal state of La Guaira, Venezuelan parliament chief Jorge Rodriguez wrote on Telegram. Thousands more are listed as missing. A 7.5-magnitude quake – the biggest in Venezuela in over a century – struck 39 seconds after a 7.2-magnitude shock, flattening entire high-rise apartment blocks. Although rescue teams have halted searches for survivors, family members continue to scour the ruins for their loved ones, in the hope of giving them a dignified burial.

At least 920 people have been confirmed dead and tens of thousands remain missing in the aftermath of a powerful double earthquake in Venezuela. The magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes – the most powerful earthquakes to hit the country in more than a century – struck within 39 seconds of each other west of the capital Caracas. Acting president Delcy Rodriguez said on Friday that at least 2,980 people had been injured, while nearly 50,000 remain missing. Ms Rodriguez said that La Guaira, the coastal state that took the brunt of the devastation, would be put under military control in an effort to cope with the disaster. The area is located approximately 20 miles (30km) away from Caracas, which was also hit by the quakes.

On Friday, a 3.0-magnitude quake in central Caracas caused momentary panic and led to buildings being evacuated. The scale of the recovery effort facing Venezuela, where state services have been severely degraded by a prolonged economic crisis, is huge. The United Nations on Wednesday issued an urgent appeal for nearly $300m towards earthquake relief operations to assist 1.3 million people in urgent need of aid in the South American country where non-governmental organisations until recently were targets of government repression. Mobile kitchens and clinics as well as field hospitals now dot public spaces in the northern state of La Guaira, where most of the devastation occurred. The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction has estimated direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure around $37bn.
